title: Rotation Angle of a Rolling Circular Wheel
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: A circular wheel with a diameter of 1 m rolls forward without slipping a distance of 30 cm along flat ground. Through what angle does the wheel rotate? State the answer in radians (to the nearest tenth) and in degrees (to the nearest degree).

steps.title: Express the Wheel Radius and Distance Rolled in Consistent Units
steps.mathExpression: d = 1\text{ m} = 100\text{ cm} \implies r = 50\text{ cm}, \quad s = 30\text{ cm}
steps.explanation: Convert the 1-meter diameter to 100 cm so that the radius r = 50 cm matches the unit of the forward rolling distance s = 30 cm.
steps.why: When a wheel rolls without slipping, the linear distance traveled equals the arc length along its rim.

steps.title: Find the Angle of Rotation in Radians
steps.explanation: Divide the arc length s = 30 cm by the radius r = 50 cm to obtain the exact rotation angle of 0.6 radians.
steps.why: The central angle in radians is the dimensionless ratio of arc length to radius.

steps.title: Convert the Rotation Angle to Degrees
steps.explanation: Multiply 0.6 radians by 180^circ/pi to obtain approximately 34.38 degrees, which rounds to 34 degrees to the nearest degree.
steps.why: Multiplying radians by 180/pi converts the angular measure into degrees.
